prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner site that teaches in plain English and uses concrete numbers in examples, or (B) a site that openly publishes its own trading losses or shows the real dollar amounts lost in hacks/exploits? Very few mainstream beginner sites publish their own P&L (personal trading losses) because of legal/risk reasons. If you tell me which you mean I can narrow it down.

Quick answer and options depending on what you meant:

If you want plain‑English beginner lessons that use real numbers and examples
- Coinbase Learn — very beginner friendly, short lessons with concrete examples and calculators. No trading P&L disclosure.
- Binance Academy — clear explainers, charts and worked examples for concepts like swaps, staking, yield.
- Coin Bureau (site + YouTube) — long, plain-English deep dives into projects with numbers and comparisons; editorial but they don’t publish personal trading losses.
- Decrypt — news + explainers written for non‑technical readers, with numeric examples.

If you want transparency about actual losses (protocol hacks, exploits, real dollars lost)
- Rekt (rekt.news / Twitter) — catalogs DeFi exploits and post‑mortems with exact loss amounts; excellent if you want to see “what went wrong” with real numbers.
- DeFiLlama / Dune Analytics dashboards — live on‑chain data and dashboards showing TVL, flows, and specific contract losses if you dig into the queries.
- The Defiant / The Block — reporting on hacks and financial hits with quantitative detail.

If you specifically want creators who publish their own trading results (including losses)
- Very few reputable educational sites do this. Some independent YouTubers/newsletters occasionally publish performance reports, but that is uncommon and often unreliable. Be cautious: published P&L can be selective or audited only rarely.

My recommendation for a sensible combo: use a plain‑English site for learning basics (Coinbase Learn or Coin Bureau) and pair it with Rekt + Dune/DeFiLlama to study real losses and on‑chain numbers. If you mean something else, tell me which type of “losses” you want and I’ll give a tighter recommendation.
